name: Server Load
description: The load on each server affects the responsiveness and timing of the coin flip. Higher load could delay the response, leading to a longer latency.

name: Network Latency
description: The network path between the controller and the servers can introduce variable latencies. Uneven network conditions could result in multimodal latency patterns.

name: Clock Synchronization
description: Differences in clock synchronization between servers can cause discrepancies in timing, especially if the servers are geographically distant.

name: Power Supply Stability
description: Variations in power supply stability can affect the performance of the servers, leading to inconsistent latencies.

name: Thermal Conditions
description: Temperature changes can impact the performance of hardware components, potentially leading to variations in processing speed and response time.

name: Software Version Differences
description: If different versions of the software are running on each server, this can introduce variability in how the consensus protocol is executed.

name: Cache Usage
description: Cache usage patterns can differ between servers, leading to varying latencies. This is especially true if the shared coin protocol relies heavily on cache hits.

name: Disk I/O Performance
description: If the servers need to access disk I/O for the shared coin mechanism, differences in disk performance could cause multimodal latencies.

name: Memory Bandwidth
description: Memory bandwidth differences can affect the speed at which data is processed, leading to varying latencies.

name: Interference from Other Processes
description: Other processes running on the servers could be interfering with the coin flip mechanism, leading to unpredictable latencies.

name: Hardware Differences
description: Differences in hardware components between the two servers could lead to variations in performance and latency.

name: Network Congestion
description: Network congestion can introduce variability in latency, especially if the network path is shared with other traffic.

name: Load Balancer Configuration
description: If a load balancer is used, its configuration could affect the distribution of requests and thus the observed latencies.

name: Operating System Configuration
description: Different configurations of the operating system could lead to variations in how the servers handle tasks and respond to requests.

name: External Interference
description: External factors such as power outages, environmental disturbances, or other external systems could affect the servers, leading to inconsistent latencies.
